headline: The rates reprieve got handed straight to the dollar — DXY at a 52-week high, and the rest of the world is paying for it.
summary: Yesterday's story was a bond-vol break; today's is a dollar squeeze. DXY +0.5% to 102.39 sits at the 100th percentile of 52 weeks with z=1.63 and acceleration 1.44 — both higher than yesterday. EURUSD 1.1184 is at the 0th percentile (-3.7% on the month, acceleration -1.60). The pressure is broad, not a euro story: USDCHF +2.7% on the month, USDCAD z=1.70 with acceleration 1.61, USDINR 96.775 at the 99th percentile with z=1.85 and acceleration 1.82, and USDMXN now the most extreme FX print on the board at z=2.59, acceleration 2.16. The first casualties are offshore equities: Euro Stoxx -1.7%, DAX -1.4%, CAC -1.1%, KOSPI -2.0%, Nikkei -0.9%, Hang Seng -0.6%, with EFA/SPY at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks (-5.1% on the month, acceleration -1.56). The dollar composite worsened to -21.

US rates improved at the margin but the damage levels are intact, and the shape changed. The front end did the work: 2y -10bp on the week to 4.79%, while the 30y is +5bp on the week to 5.64% at the 98th percentile and the 10y is +1bp to 5.27% at the 97th. 2s10s +11bp on the week to 48bp — this is a steepener, not a rally. The 10-year real yield is still 2.91% with z=1.88 and acceleration 1.35, the 30-year mortgage is 7.28% at the 100th percentile and +62bp on the month, and MOVE at 105.2 still carries z=2.40 in the 83rd percentile. Rates composite -80, barely off yesterday's -85. A 10bp week in 2s does not undo a 49bp month in 10s.

Risk appetite is being bled out quietly rather than violently. VIX +6.1% to 15.92 is the first tick up, and it still only sits at the 14th percentile with VIX3M at the 2nd and SKEW -6.8% on the month with acceleration -1.90 — equity tails keep getting cheaper while bond vol sits two standard deviations rich. Breadth is the worst number on the page: RSP/SPY at the 3.9th percentile (z=-1.87), IWM/SPY -6.0% on the month, transports/S&P and retail/S&P both at the 0th percentile. The monetary-metal unwind accelerated again with the dollar — gold -1.1% to 4,142.7 and -7.5% on the month (z=-1.80, acceleration -1.69), silver -8.6% and platinum -9.6% on the month, GDX -11.1% with acceleration -2.04 — and crypto finally cracked: BTC -2.3%, ETH -4.6%, SOL -3.0% after +50.6% over three months. Risk regime -12.

What's holding this together is credit and the AI complex, and nothing today challenged either. HYG +0.4% with HYG/IEF at the 99th percentile and +1.1% on the month, BKLN at the 95th, credit composite 41 — the pain is discount-rate pain, not default pain. Leadership is narrow and still working: CIBR +14.3% on the month at a 52-week high with acceleration 1.77, SOXX +13.5%, SMH +11.6%, AMD +36.0%, META +19.9%, TSM +12.7%, high-beta/low-vol at the 99.6th percentile. Against that, the capital-markets complex is in open liquidation into earnings — GS -13.6% on the month (z=-1.97), BX -16.7%, IAI -9.3% (z=-1.77), XLF -6.7% with -8.0% relative strength — and EM is splitting cleanly along its currencies: Brazil is the only thing working (EWZ +17.9% on the week, BVSP z=1.90, USDBRL -4.3%) while India (INDA -6.4% month, 5th percentile), Turkey (-12.1%) and South Africa (-11.1%) go out with their FX.

good.text: Credit still refuses to participate in the stress: HYG +0.4%, HYG/IEF at the 99th percentile of 52 weeks and +1.1% on the month, BKLN at the 95th. Credit composite 41 — this is a rotation, not a regime break.

Copper/gold broke to a fresh 52-week high, +8.7% on the month with z=1.25 and acceleration 1.42, copper +0.7% to 6.639 and Brent +1.3% to 101.88. The real-economy pulse is firming even as monetary metals get liquidated; growth composite +15.

The AI/cyber leadership block is accelerating, not fading: CIBR +14.3% on the month at the 100th percentile with acceleration 1.77, SOXX +13.5%, SMH +11.6%, AMD +36.0% (z=1.78), TSM +12.7%, IGV +5.6% on the week. SMH/SPY and high-beta/low-vol both near 52-week highs.
The front end finally gave something back: 2y -10bp on the week to 4.79%, 3m bill -4bp, MOVE -7.4% off its extreme. Rates composite improved to -80 from -85.

Inflation inputs are inert to softening despite the oil bid: 5y breakeven 2.37% with acceleration -0.61, 10y breakeven 2.36%, RBOB -7.9% on the week and -1.5% on the month. The yield problem is term premium, not expected CPI.

Brazil is the one EM trade compounding: EWZ +17.9% on the week and +13.6% on the month (z=1.55), BVSP z=1.90 at the 98th percentile, USDBRL -4.3% on the week to 4.98. Strong currency plus strong index is the rare combination on this page.

bad.text: Dollar breakout is the new tightening: DXY 102.39 at the 100th percentile with z=1.63 and acceleration 1.44, EURUSD at the 0th percentile, USDMXN z=2.59/acc 2.16, USDINR at the 99th percentile. Accelerating here is unambiguously bad — it drains EM and offshore earnings.
Non-US equities broke on the dollar move: Euro Stoxx -1.7%, DAX -1.4%, CAC -1.1% (6.4% month loss, 10th percentile), KOSPI -2.0%, Nikkei -0.9%. EFA/SPY at the 0th percentile with acceleration -1.56.

Breadth keeps rotting under a 100th-percentile index: RSP/SPY at the 3.9th percentile (z=-1.87, acceleration -1.23), IWM/SPY -6.0% on the month, transports/S&P and retail/S&P both pinned at the 0th percentile. Breadth composite -14.

The long end is doing the damage even as the front end eases: 30y 5.64% (+5bp on the week, 98th percentile), 10y real yield 2.91% with z=1.88 and acceleration 1.35, 30-year mortgage 7.28% at the 100th percentile and +62bp on the month. Housing is still being strangled — ITB -6.6% on the month, XHB/SPY at the 1st percentile.

Hedges have never been cheaper against the most unstable rate tape in a year: VIX 15.92 at the 14th percentile, VIX3M at the 2nd, SKEW -6.8% on the month with acceleration -1.90, while MOVE holds z=2.40 in the 83rd percentile. Today's +6.1% VIX tick is the first warning shot.

Capital markets are being liquidated into earnings season: GS -13.6% on the month (z=-1.97), BX -16.7% (z=-1.74), IAI -9.3% (z=-1.77, acceleration -1.39), KBE -7.3%, XLF relative strength -8.0%. Steeper curve has not bought the banks a bid.

trades.name: Buy cheap S&P downside vs rich bond vol
trades.line: Own SPY Dec puts/VIX calls — equity tails vs MOVE z=2.4
trades.expr: Buy SPY Dec-26 5% OTM puts or a 1x2 put spread; alternatively VIX Dec 20/30 call spreads. Funded by selling upside calls in the index, not in semis.
trades.thesis: Bond vol is priced two standard deviations rich while equity vol is priced at the 2nd-14th percentile. That gap closes through equity vol, not through bonds, and the dollar move adds a second transmission channel.
trades.trigger: VIX +6.1% to 15.92 today — its first up-tick — while VIX3M sits at the 1.9th percentile and SKEW is -6.8% on the month with acceleration -1.90, against MOVE 105.2 at z=2.40 and a 10y real yield at z=1.88.
trades.stop: VIX3M back below 16 with MOVE under 95 and RSP/SPY reclaiming its 200-day — i.e. real yields fall and breadth repairs together.
trades.target: VIX 22-25 / VIX3M above 22; pays 3-5x on the call spread.

trades.name: Long SPY vs short EFA
trades.line: Short developed ex-US, long S&P: dollar does the work
trades.expr: Long SPY, short EFA, dollar-neutral notional. Sizing 1:1; can substitute short EWG/EWU for a cleaner Europe tilt.
trades.thesis: A dollar breaking to a 52-week high with acceleration 1.44 is a direct tax on unhedged ex-US equity in USD terms, and European indices are already rolling on their own.
trades.trigger: DXY +0.5% to 102.39 at the 100th percentile, EURUSD at the 0th; Euro Stoxx -1.7%, DAX -1.4%, CAC -1.1% today; EFA/SPY at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks, -5.1% on the month with acceleration -1.56.
trades.stop: DXY back below 100.5 (z under 1.0) or EFA/SPY closing above its 200-day — either kills the dollar leg.
trades.target: Another 5% on the ratio; EFA/SPY toward 0.127.

trades.name: Fade the housing bounce (ITB)
trades.line: Short ITB into the rate-relief pop; mortgage still 7.28%
trades.expr: Short ITB outright, or buy Jan ITB puts ~8% OTM. Pair-hedge with long SPY if you want the relative version (XHB/SPY).
trades.thesis: Builders rallied on a 4bp day in 10s while the variable that actually matters — the 30-year mortgage — sits at a 52-week high and is still accelerating. Affordability has not improved; positioning just got squeezed.
trades.trigger: ITB +1.6% and XHB +1.1% yesterday on the rates reprieve, but MORTGAGE30US 7.28% is at the 100th percentile, +62bp on the month with acceleration 1.27, 30y yield +5bp on the week to 5.64%, and ITB is -6.6% on the month with XHB/SPY at the 1.3rd percentile.
trades.stop: 30-year mortgage back under 6.90% or 30y Treasury below 5.35%; cover.

trades.name: Long copper miners vs short gold miners
trades.line: COPX over GDX: copper/gold just hit a 52-week high
trades.expr: Long COPX, short GDX, equal dollar notional. Cash-commodity version: long copper futures vs short gold futures on the CU/AU ratio.
trades.thesis: The dollar breakout is killing the monetary-metal trade while the industrial-metal trade is being supported by a firming growth pulse. Own the metal that needs demand, short the metal that needed a weak dollar.
trades.trigger: Copper/gold +1.8% today to a fresh 52-week high (+8.7% on the month, z=1.25, acceleration 1.42); gold -7.5% on the month with z=-1.80 and acceleration -1.69; GDX -11.1% on the month with acceleration -2.04 and GDX/gold acceleration -2.06; copper +9.7% over three months.
trades.stop: Copper/gold back below its 200-day (ratio -8% from here) or DXY rolling under 100 and gold reclaiming 4,350.
trades.target: 10-15% on the spread; COPX relative strength vs S&P back to positive on 1m.

trades.name: Long Brazil vs short India
trades.line: EWZ over INDA — the FX decides the EM winner
trades.expr: Long EWZ, short INDA, equal notional. Scale in on EWZ pullbacks toward 41 given it is 18% above its 200-day.
trades.thesis: EM is splitting along currencies, not along growth. BRL strength is funding a genuine index breakout; INR weakness at a 99th-percentile USDINR is bleeding Indian equity in dollars.
trades.trigger: EWZ +17.9% on the week, +13.6% on the month (z=1.55) at a 52-week high with USDBRL -4.3% on the week; INDA -6.4% on the month at the 13th percentile with USDINR +2.5% on the month (z=1.85, acceleration 1.82) and Sensex at the 5th percentile.
trades.stop: USDBRL back above 5.20 or EWZ losing 10% from entry; USDINR turning below 94.
trades.target: 15% on the spread over a quarter.

trades.name: 2s30s steepener
trades.line: Long front end, short long bond: curve is the live trade
trades.expr: Buy 2y futures (ZT) vs sell ultra-bond (UB) duration-weighted; ETF proxy long SHY vs short TLT at matched DV01.
trades.thesis: The easing is happening only where the Fed controls it. Term premium at the long end is still expanding on supply and sticky real yields, so the curve does the work even if the level of yields goes nowhere.
trades.trigger: 2y -10bp on the week to 4.79% while the 30y is +5bp to 5.64% at the 98th percentile and the 10y is +1bp; 2s10s +11bp on the week to 48bp; TLT at the 1.5th percentile of 52 weeks and -5.6% on the month.
trades.stop: 2s10s back under 35bp, or the 2y yield making a new high above 4.90% (a hawkish-repricing flattening).

trades.name: Short MSTR as the crypto-beta fade
trades.line: Short MSTR: +69% in 3m into a rising dollar and ETH -4.6%
trades.expr: Short MSTR outright, or buy Nov/Dec puts ~10% OTM to cap the squeeze risk. Hedge with a small long IBIT if you want pure premium-to-NAV exposure.
trades.thesis: The crypto bounce was a weak-dollar, falling-real-yield trade. Both have reversed this week, and the leveraged proxy carries three times the beta of the underlying.
trades.trigger: MSTR +15.2% on the month and +69.0% over three months, 21% above its 200-day, while BTC -2.3%, ETH -4.6%, SOL -3.0% today and ETH/BTC -4.1% on the week; DXY at a 52-week high and the 10y real yield still z=1.88.
trades.stop: BTC closing above 90,000 or IBIT reclaiming its recent high; cover.
